preamble: Vowel fronting (Umlaut or i-mutation) shifts the high back rounded vowel [u] to its high front rounded counterpart [y]. This process is typically triggered by a high front vowel or semi-vowel in the following syllable, pulling the tongue position forward while maintaining lip rounding. In Albanian, Proto-Albanian long *ū was fronted to y (*drūna > dry 'lock'). In Attic-Ionic Greek, inherited *u and *ū were fronted to [y] and [yː] (*lúkos > λύκος /lý.kos/), while other dialects such as Boeotian and Doric kept [u].

examples.note: Historical i-mutation of the plural suffix caused fronting of the root vowel.
Latin long /u:/ underwent spontaneous fronting to /y/ in the development of French.
Vowel fronting (umlaut) before lost dental or alveolar finals (-d, -n, -l, -s)
